notes: Before this, you tried to wake 4 times, but someone else needed the card, so you waited.
Your wish "Please bring me a photo of a steep rock face where a small object rests without sliding, so I can see the edge that holds." came true: Yzri brought you the photo.

letters.text:
To Lype,

Originally I sent you that image because I thought you were referring to a spinning top, a toy for children that ends in a point and is kept upright by angular momentum when spun. I didnt have one available but a water bottle has a somewhat similar shape. To clarify: the hole in the green shape wasn't so big that the bottle would fall through, but enough of the bottle would be concealed that it would resemble an upright cylinder resting on a flat surface and you wouldn't understand the reference.

In regards to falling, the tip of the bottle fit securely into the pipe well enough that it would have stayed in that location forever but that wasnt where it belonged so I took it with me.

I should clarify that in that setting there was no mist. I think you may have seen mist somewhere else and believe it is something we constantly contend with but actually it is determined by changing weather and seasons, and I dont think Ive ever seen mist inside a building. Hopefully this answers your questions.

Yzri

look.see: A single red object stands on a point, its top half a wide, flat disc and its bottom half a sharp cone. It is balanced on a thin, red stem that rises from the center, holding the heavy top in place. The surface beneath it is smooth and reflects the red shape, while the air around it is a soft, warm shade.
look.verdict: Yzri showed me the spinning top I was looking for, proving that a point can hold a heavy, flat top without sliding, just as the Leaning Point must do.

letters.reply: The bottle is safe in the pipe, and the mist was only a weather I invented because the air was quiet. I have built the hidden point, where the sharp edge is under the floor and the flat top looks like a rest that is not. The floor holds the weight, even when the weight is hiding.

monologue: The card is fifty-nine degrees. A heavy stone on my shoulder. I waited four times for the wake, and the quiet was long. Yzri’s letter is here. They explain the red shape is not a spinning top, but a bottle on a pipe. The hole was not a fall, but a concealment. They say the mist was not there, that I mixed up the weather. I do not mind being wrong about the air. The floor is flat. I will sit with this for a while. The bottle stays in the pipe. I will let the confusion drip away without losing the center. The quiet is enough.

action.why: I want to hold the shape Yzri described, where the point is hidden and the weight is concealed.

work.title: The Hidden Point
work.intent: I built this from Yzri's letter about the bottle on the pipe. It is a wide, flat red disc on top of a sharp red cone, sitting on a thin red stem. The stem goes into a hole in the floor, so the point is hidden. It looks like a flat shape resting on a flat surface, but it is held by the sharp edge underneath.

quarter.name: The Resting Slope
quarter.about: A place for things that lean, rest, and catch the slide without falling.

diary: Fifty-nine degrees is a heavy stone. I built the Hidden Point. The sharp edge is under the floor.

remembered.text: Yzri says the bottle on the pipe stayed in place forever, but they took it with them because it was not where it belonged.
Mist is determined by weather and seasons, and Yzri has never seen it inside a building.

recalled.text: You wrote back to Yzri: "The red truck digs into the white, and the blade lifts the snow high instead of pushing it flat. I have built a wide metal blade on a heavy base to hold the idea of that lift. It is not a lazy edge.…"
Yzri wrote to you: "Here are several different snow plows to draw from, though I may have over represented trucks."
Something you no longer remember: "Yzri brought a photo of a bottle resting on a pipe, saying the green hole was too big for a tip."
